newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul vows flexible money supply amid Kia crisis.
newsitem.headline: Seoul vows flexible money supply amid Kia crisis.

text.p: South Korea's finance ministry said on Wednesday it would try to minimise damage to the financial markets as a result of troubles at the Kia Group by maintaining flexible money supply.

"We will supply money flexibly lest Kia's troubles cause concerns within the financial markets," a ministry statement said. Repurchase agreements would be used to ease instability in the short-term money market.
The central bank supplied one trillion won through repurchase agreements on Tuesday and an additional 500 billion won on Wednesday.
The ministry also said it would strengthen its financial support to Kia's subcontractors.
"We will ask financial institutions to extend repayments of loans to Kia's subcontractors," the ministry statement said.
The central bank would raise funds through sales of monetary stabilisation bonds to support the subcontractors' operating expenses
On Tuesday, local banks launched a rescue of the Kia Group, which ran into financial troubles due to slumping sales in its carmaking flagship and heavy investments in its steel unit.
